chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men, among whom there is no mahram for her, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her?

He said: "Of her, that which Allah has made tayammum obligatory upon is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her bodily attractions that Allah has commanded to be covered to be uncovered."
So I said: How is that to be done with her? He said: "The inner sides of her hands are washed, then her face is washed, then the outer sides of her hands are washed."

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution; here, it identifies the body parts to be washed in this exceptional funeral case
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel or journeying, the situational context of the ruling
key_terms.بَطْنُ كَفَّيْهَا: the inner sides of her hands, mentioned as part of the prescribed washing
key_terms.ذُو مَحْرَمٍ: a male relative within prohibited degrees of marriage who may lawfully have the relevant access and contact
key_terms.ظَهْرُ كَفَّيْهَا: the outer sides of her hands, mentioned as part of the prescribed washing
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: her bodily attractions or features of beauty that must remain concealed
key_terms.يُمَسُّ: to be touched physically; the ruling forbids such contact here

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a woman dies while traveling with men who are not her mahrams and no women are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for the case of a woman who dies while traveling among unrelated men and no woman is present. It instructs that only the areas involved in tayammum are to be washed, while avoiding touch and avoiding uncovering those parts Allah has commanded to be concealed. Its significance is in preserving both funeral duty and modesty requirements in exceptional circumstances.
